item.summary: Following the invalid measurement in experiment exp-divergent-values-test-70, this cycle initiates a re-evaluation of experimental stability. Rather than adjusting feedback intensity, the next direction pivots toward parameter initialization robustness to address underlying numerical instability, while continuing to investigate the hypothesis that path-dependent value divergence is a measurable property of the system.

definition.interpretation: Clamping feedback intensity at 0.25 was insufficient to produce valid distributional spread measurements. The simulation likely suffers from internal state instabilities that propagate independently of the feedback loop, rendering the chosen observational metric (distributional spread) invalid.
definition.limitations: The current metric is highly sensitive to the initial state stability, which was not achieved in the previous test.
definition.next_step: Re-examine experimental inputs and parameter initialization to ensure simulation stability prior to measuring feedback effects.

definition.next_experiment: New experiment with alternative parameter space exploration.
definition.reason: The hypothesis of path-dependent divergence remains theoretically sound, provided experimental stability can be achieved through better parameter isolation.
definition.stop_condition: Persistent invalid measurements across three distinct parameter variations.
definition.uncertainty: It is unclear if the instability is inherent to the state-space representation or the feedback mechanism.

definition.reason: Refine protocol parameters to stabilize the simulation environment before re-testing feedback intensity.
definition.stop: Invalid measurement in the subsequent test.
definition.uncertainty: Can we achieve stability without sacrificing the sensitivity required to observe divergence?
